_doc: One file per place. build.py renders /states/<slug>/ (kind=state) or /countries/<slug>/ (kind=country) from this file. Every number must be an official published figure with its source. Amounts in US dollars. Headline is Census state + local debt (same source and definition for every state); the state's own fresher, narrower figure is the secondary line.
name: Florida
title: Florida Debt Clock: Live State and Local Debt, From Official Data
cadence: Annual. The Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances comes out about two years after the fiscal year (survey year 2024: July 2026; survey year 2023: July 2025).
next_update: The next Census figures, for survey year 2025, are expected around mid-2027, based on the last two release dates. The state's own report (shown as a secondary line) updates sooner.
fiscal_year_end_note: Florida's fiscal year ends June 30. Census survey year 2024 covers each government's fiscal year that ended between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2024; the clock dates it June 30, 2024, the end of that window.

population.source_name: Census Bureau, Vintage 2025 state population estimates (NST-EST2025)

components.label: State government debt
components.source_name: US Census Bureau, Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, table GS00LOCALFIN (State and Local Government Finances by Level of Government: U.S. and States: 2017-2024), Debt - Total Debt Outstanding (LF0231)
components.source_locator: Florida, Government type 'State', items LF0231 Total, LF0233 Long-term and LF0232 Short-term Debt Outstanding, survey year 2024; amounts published in $1,000
components.includes: All debt of the Florida state government as Census defines it: long-term and short-term debt of the state and its dependent agencies, whatever the source of repayment. Census uses the same definition for every state.

components.label: Local government debt
components.source_name: US Census Bureau, Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, table GS00LOCALFIN (State and Local Government Finances by Level of Government: U.S. and States: 2017-2024), Debt - Total Debt Outstanding (LF0231)
components.source_locator: Florida, Government type 'Local', items LF0231 Total, LF0233 Long-term and LF0232 Short-term Debt Outstanding, survey year 2024; amounts published in $1,000
components.includes: All debt of Florida's counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts, on the same Census definition. Census estimates local totals from a sample of local governments in most years (2022 was a full count, the Census of Governments); coefficient of variation for 2024: 2.31%.

secondary.label: State's own report: state direct debt
secondary.publisher: Florida Division of Bond Finance, 2025 Debt Report
secondary.scope: Narrower scope and a year newer: the State's direct debt only (tax-supported plus self-supporting), no local debt and no indirect debt. It has been falling while local debt rises. Not added to the total.
secondary.source_name: Florida Division of Bond Finance, 2025 State of Florida Debt Report (Dec 2025), Direct Debt Outstanding by Type and Program
secondary.source_locator: Direct Debt Outstanding by Type and Program, as of June 30, 2025, printed page 6 (PDF page 9); $ millions
secondary.includes: Direct debt repaid from state taxes and appropriations: education, environmental, transportation (including $2.46 billion of public-private partnership obligations) and appropriated debt. Direct debt repaid from the revenue of the financed project: toll roads and university facilities.

notes: Census publishes Florida's state + local total as $132.57 billion for 2024 (coefficient of variation 1.96%) and $131.12 billion for 2023. State + local here is exactly Census's state figure plus its local figure.

Census's figures are the newest official state + local totals that use one definition for all 50 states, but they lag about two years, so the page shows the official figure as of June 30, 2024. The state's own report (Florida Division of Bond Finance, 2025 Debt Report) is fresher but narrower; it is shown separately and never added. Census does not publish a reconciliation to state reports, so we do not itemize the gap.

The 2023→2024 change (+$1.45 billion) is smaller than about two standard errors of the Census estimate (about $5.2 billion at a 1.96% coefficient of variation), so Census's data does not show which way the debt is moving. This page therefore shows the official figure as published and does not tick it forward.

About the state's own figure: Not included: local government debt; indirect debt (about $12.6 billion); university direct-support-organization debt; unfunded pension and retiree-health liabilities; and Florida's share of the federal debt.
Not included: unfunded pension and retiree-health liabilities, and the state's share of the federal debt.
legend: Florida state + local debt is reported once a year by the Census Bureau, about two years after the fact. Real borrowing happens in lumps when bonds are sold and is repaid on schedules, so the page shows the latest official figure without ticking it forward, because Census's own sampling error is larger than the change it measured.
